correctness.rationale: For each unit row, the orthogonal error projector is a rank-one tangent projector. Its sweep product has norm equal to the product of cosines of consecutive angular differences, proving exact zero iff some adjacent pair is orthogonal. The even frame orthogonality graph is a perfect matching; the odd minimizer equality graph is one modular cycle, with exactly 2n Hamiltonian orders. Fixed-matching block compression yields exact joint factorial moments and binomial inversion; finite-order asymptotics are supported by an absolutely summable factorial expansion. Independent draws have exactly independent conditional orthogonal-pair hits and tight-frame mean-square factor one-half per step. The package verifier enumerates 87320 finite assertions, but infinite statements follow from the proof only.

originality.rationale: The identical EVEN equispaced frame is prior art (Oswald–Zhou 2015, their equation (18)); only the exact uniformly reshuffled one-epoch zero-operator distribution, sharp comparison to independent sampling and all deterministic optimum orders are proposed as new here. Checked primary theory and closest published exact benchmarks do not state or imply these exact claims. The inclusion–exclusion counting method, general orthogonality ordering ideas and the geometry itself are known. This is best-knowledge originality, not independently certified priority.

value.rationale: The exact event of finite termination in one complete randomly shuffled sweep is a natural reliability invariant for a canonical tight planar equation frame. It has a new-looking parity boundary with nontrivial limiting mass on the even side, a full finite distribution and sharp difference from same-cost independent sampling, plus complete globally optimal deterministic permutations. This resolves a precise solver-order design problem rather than computing an arbitrary isolated probability. The baseline geometry, cyclic ordering and general combinatorial methods are credited prior art, and robustness is explicitly not claimed.
